en: Price tenders, compare quotes and control contracts in one workbook
Price tenders, compare quotes and control contracts
Estimate lines priced by cost code
quantity times labour, material and plant rates for every line; the tender sums them into the direct cost without retyping
every tender shows its price, direct cost, margin and a status that warns before a deadline and flags a price below your minimum margin
Subcontractor quotes ranked in each package
quotes are ranked, compared with the package average and marked as ended when they are no longer valid
Unit rate library with rate age
labour, material and plant per unit give the cost and the price with overhead and profit, and old rates are flagged for review
chance times cost for each risk gives the allowance to carry in the price, with a level for high and medium risks
Contract register with retention and damages
value, retention held, defects period end, payment days and the cap on delay damages for every contract
each milestone shows its share of the value, the amount, the days late and whether it is overdue
amount, premium and days left for every bond and cover, with a warning before it ends
Win rate by project kind and month
tenders won and lost, value won and average margin by kind and by month show where you win and where you only spend time
Lost tenders and the gap to the winner
each loss records the reason and the winning price, and shows how far your price was above it
five scores for each lead give a total and a clear decision against your pass mark
Target margin on the tender price
Yearly price rise to allow for
Days before a tender deadline to warn you
Days before a bond or insurance ends to warn you
Days after which a unit rate needs review
Yearly turnover you want from contracts
Bid review score needed to bid (out of 25)
Your cost of money, per year
Cap on delay damages, share of contract value
Days without contact before a client needs a call
Expected cost of a high risk
Expected cost of a medium risk
Your cost to prepare one tender
Clients and what you have tendered and built for them
One row for each client; leads, tenders, wins, win rate, tendered value and contract value fill in from the other sheets.
One row for each person you deal with at a client, their role and whether they sign off; days since contact and a reminder to call fill in.
Leads and enquiries before you decide to tender
One row for each enquiry with its source, estimated value, stage and next follow-up date; age, follow-up status and the client phone fill in.
Score each lead from 1 to 5 on fit, capacity, margin, risk and relationship; the total and the decision against your pass mark fill in.
Tender register: deadline, price, result and margin
One row for each tender with its deadline, price and result; direct cost comes from the estimate lines, then margin, days left and a status that warns about deadlines fill in.
Estimate lines by cost code: quantity times unit rates
One row for each estimate line with quantity and the labour, material and plant rate for each unit; the cost of each part and the line total fill in, and the tender sums them.
Unit rate library with labour, material and plant
One row for each type of work with its labour, material and plant cost for one unit and a waste allowance; the cost for one unit and the price with overhead and profit fill in.
Labour rates by trade with on-costs
One row for each trade with the hourly wage, overtime factor and on-costs; the loaded hour, the cost of a working day and the overtime hour fill in.
Material price list with the latest change
One row for each material with the supplier, the current and previous price; the change and whether the price is rising fill in.
Plant and equipment rates: owned and hired
One row for each machine with day rate, operator, fuel and moving cost; the all-in day, the week rate with your discount and moving in and out fill in.
Subcontractor quotes compared for each package
One row for each quote; the rank in its package, the average of the package, the difference from the average and whether the quote is still valid fill in.
One row for each visit with access, ground, power, hazards and the extra cost to allow for; a status shows which sites need an allowance in the price.
Risks and allowances priced for each tender
One row for each risk with its chance and cost; the expected cost to carry in the price and a risk level fill in.
One row for each item that states what the price leaves out, assumes or holds as a provisional sum; a status shows whether it is priced.
Contract register: value, type, retention and terms
One row for each contract with value, dates, retention, payment terms, defects period and delay damages; the retention held, the defects end date and the phase fill in.
Contract milestones and the price each releases
One row for each milestone with its due date, share of the contract value and the date achieved; the amount, delay and status fill in.
Insurance and bonds for each contract
One row for each bond or insurance with its provider, amount, dates and premium rate; the days left, the premium and a warning before it ends fill in.
Lost tenders and why you lost
One row for each lost tender with the reason and the winning price; your price, the gap to the winner and the client fill in.
Win rate by project kind and period
One row for each project kind and period you want to study; tenders decided, won, lost, the win rate and the value won fill in from the register.
One row for each month; tenders due, submitted, won and lost, the win rate, the value tendered and won and the average margin fill in from the register.
Tenders due in the next 14 days
Tenders past the deadline, not submitted
Direct cost in tenders waiting or open
Expected cost of the risks you priced
Quotes that are the lowest in a package
Site visits that need an allowance
Retention at most, contracts in progress
Tenders, leads and milestones by month
Tender summary with its estimate lines
Subcontractor quote comparison for a tender
Bid or no bid review sheet
Estimate builder: direct cost to tender price
Type the labour, material, plant and subcontract cost; see the contingency, overhead, profit, the tender price and the margin, next to the margin you have really made on won tenders.
Average margin on your won tenders
Type your cost and either a markup on cost or the margin you want on price; see the price both ways and the markup that gives your target margin.
Tender price check before you submit
Type the price, the direct cost and the risk allowance; see the margin, whether it meets your minimum and target and the price you need.
Margin after the risk allowance is used
Overhead recovery: what percentage covers the office
Type your yearly office overheads and the direct cost you expect to build; see the overhead percentage every tender must carry and what you lose if you price below it.
Direct cost you expect to build in the year
Share of your overhead you fail to recover
Shortfall or surplus at your setting
Direct cost you must win to recover the overheads
Overhead on each estimate you tendered
Unit rate builder for one unit of work
Type the crew hours, wage, material and plant for one unit; see the cost and price of one unit and of the whole quantity.
Price of one unit with overhead and profit
Labour hours for the whole quantity
Contingency sizing from the risks you priced
Type the direct cost and a tender number; see the expected cost of its risks, the contingency that covers them and how it compares with your standard percentage.
Share of expected risk cost to cover
Expected cost of the risks in the register
Contingency as a share of cost
Score a new enquiry from 1 to 5 on five questions; see the total, your pass mark and the advice.
Points above or below the mark
Reviews that passed in your register
Type the contract value and months; see how much you normally build by each quarter of the time, the busiest month and the retention held halfway.
Share built by 25% of the time
Retention held at the halfway point
Retention cost: what money held back costs you
Type the contract value, retention, months and months until release; see the most that is held, the average held and what financing it costs.
Months to wait after completion for release
Average retention held during the build
Cost as a share of the contract value
Retention held now across your contracts
Type the contract value, the damages for each day and the days you expect to be late; see the damages, the cap and the days until the cap is reached.
Days until the cap is reached
Damages as a share of the value
Damages cap across your contracts in progress
Type the cost, the months until you buy and the yearly price rise; see the allowance to add and the price rises your own material list shows.
Average latest change in your material prices
Win rate needed for your target turnover
Type the turnover you want and the size of an average contract; see the contracts to win, the tenders to submit at your real win rate and what preparing them costs.
Tenders you can prepare in the year
Tenders to submit at your real win rate
Type up to four quotes for a package; see the lowest, the average, the spread and how far the next quote is from the lowest.
Gap you accept for a better rated sub
Quotes within the accepted gap of the lowest
Most you pay for a better rated sub
Type the date you receive the documents and the working days for each step; see the dates to visit the site, send quote requests, finish the price and submit.
Working days to the site visit
Working days to send quote requests
Working days to finish the price
Working days for the review before submitting
Thank a client for the invitation
Hello {name}, thank you for inviting us to tender. We will send our price by the deadline. Call us if anything changes.
Check in with a past client
Hello {name}, we hope your project is going well. If you plan new work, we would be glad to price it.
Ask a contact for a short call
Hello {name}, it has been {days_since} days since we spoke. Do you have 10 minutes this week to talk about your plans?
Invite a decision maker to meet
Hello {name}, we would like to present our experience on similar projects. When can we meet at your office or on site?
Hello, thank you for your enquiry about "{project}". We will review the documents and come back to you within two working days.
Hello, we are following up on "{project}". Can you confirm the tender deadline and send the drawings and the specification?
Hello, to price "{project}" correctly we would like to visit the site. Which day and time suits you this week?
Hello, thank you for inviting us to tender for "{project}". Our team is fully booked, so we must decline this time. We hope to work with you later.
Hello, we submitted our tender for "{project}" with a price of {bid}. Please tell us when you expect a decision.
Hello, we are pricing "{project}" and need an answer to a question about the drawings. The deadline is {deadline}. When can we talk?
Hello, we ask for a short extension of the deadline of {deadline} for "{project}" so that we can price it with firm subcontractor quotes.
Hello, we are waiting for the result of the tender for "{project}" at {bid}. Is there any news or a question about our price?
Thank a client for the award
Hello, thank you for awarding us "{project}". We will send the contract documents and a start plan this week.
Ask for a debrief after a loss
Hello, thank you for the chance to tender for "{project}". Could you tell us how our price compared and what we can do better next time?
Extend the validity of a price
Hello, our price of {bid} for "{project}" is still open. Please tell us if you need it to stay valid for longer.
Hello, we invite you to quote for the {package} package of "{proj}". Please send your price by {valid} with your inclusions and exclusions.
Remind a subcontractor of a quote
Hello, a reminder for your quote for {package} on "{proj}". We close our price soon. Can you send it today?
Tell a subcontractor you plan to use it
Hello, we plan to use your quote of {amount} for {package} on "{proj}" if we win the contract. We will send the subcontract soon.
Tell a subcontractor they lost the quote
Hello, thank you for quoting for {package} on "{proj}". We chose another quote this time. We will invite you again.
Ask for a quote to stay valid
Hello, your quote for {package} on "{proj}" ended on {valid}. Can you confirm that the price of {amount} still holds?
